articles.title: Bitcoin's rally following the Nvidia news proved short-lived, as the macro backdrop remains negative
articles.description: Bitcoin spiked to the upside yesterday after the news of Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO triggered a strong rally in equity markets. The news helped reset the sentiment, which got very bearish in the final part of last week. But it didn’t really change the bigger picture, which is why the gains were eventually faded. In fact, the Fed is still going to raise rates and how much will depend on the economic data and the stock market conditions. The US-Iran stalemate is still on, and the situation doesn’t look like it’s going to improve anytime soon, with Trump continuing to signal renewed military campaign in case negotiations fail. Therefore, the macro backdrop remains negative for Bitcoin and the crypto market in general, although the Nvidia news might keep the sentiment supported in the short-term. Looking ahead, Bitcoin will likely remain skewed to the downside as long as the macro conditions remain unchanged. For a reversal in the trend, we will likely need a more dovish Fed or an end to the Iran war. BITCOIN TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that Bitcoinprobed briefly below the yearly low around the 58,000 level but eventually pared back the losses. We got a pullback into a downward trendline before a rejection. The sellers will likely continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to pile in for a correction into the next downward trendline around the 70,000 level. ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the sellers will have a better risk to reward setup around the downward trendline, while the buyers will need a breakout to open the door for new highs. ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor resistance zone around the 61,000 level. The sellers will likely continue to step in around the resistance, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break to pile in for a rally into the trendline, targeting a breakout. The red lines define the average daily range for today. UPCOMING CATALYSTS Todaywe get the US Consumer Confidence report. Tomorrow, we have the US Core PCE price index and the latest US Jobless Claims figures. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

articles.title: POWERCHINA Integrates Species Protection and Wildlife Corridors into International Clean Energy Projects in Colombia and Egypt
articles.description: BEIJING, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Power Construction Corporation of China ("POWERCHINA" or "the Company") is integrating biodiversity protection into clean energy projects in Colombia and Egypt, with projects incorporating plant conservation, wildlife relocation, and habitat connectivity into daily operations. POWERCHINA Integrates Species Protection and Wildlife Corridors into International Clean Energy Projects in Colombia and Egypt Project records show that 3,382 epiphytic plants have been transplanted and 2841,186 wild animals rescued or relocated at its 250.8 MWp Santander solar project in Colombia, demonstrating how ecological management can inform construction practices across varied environments. Construction began at Santander in April 2026 and is supported by a dedicated ecological team of eight biological specialists and one veterinarian, with a 500-square-metre exclusive nursery conservation area established. The team conducts plant surveys, operates a nursery, and maintains individual records for rescued epiphytic plants. Each plant receives an identification code to support tracking through collection, nursery care, transplantation, and subsequent monitoring. To date, the project has rescued 3,382 epiphytic plants, all of which have been successfully transplanted to suitable alternative locations. Wildlife protection is similarly integrated into site operations. A professional on-site wildlife emergency rescue centre and supporting facilities are available for condition assessment, treatment, and release of injured or trapped wildlife, ensuring timely and proper handling of various ecological risks during on‑site operations. Ecological monitoring has informed measures to preserve wildlife movement across the construction site at POWERCHINA's Guayepo 3 solar project in Colombia. Using infrared camera monitoring, the project has established four dedicated wildlife passages to connect habitats separated by project infrastructure. Construction schedules also accommodate nesting birds, with affected areas protected and work suspended locally until the birds leave naturally when workers discover nests or eggs. In Egypt, POWERCHINA's 500 MW Amunet wind project applied species-specific measures to protect Egyptian spiny-tailed lizards during construction. Specialists inspect burrows, capture animals without injury, and provide temporary care before conducting phased releases into suitable habitats. Subsequent monitoring supports assessment of relocation outcomes. The project also optimizes turbine, road, and transmission-line layouts to minimize disturbance to desert surfaces and wildlife habitats. At Santander, biodiversity protection strictly follows local environmental permit requirements and the project's environmental management plan. POWERCHINA has held project briefings to keep local communities, government agencies and other stakeholders with land rights informed of the latest progress on construction plans and environmental protection measures. Meanwhile, the project carries out ecological education activities in local communities and schools to continuously raise public awareness of ecological protection and build local consensus on conservation. POWERCHINA will continue to carry out plant and wildlife stewardship, ecological monitoring, habitat restoration and other related work, deeply embedding biodiversity conservation throughout the full life cycle of international renewable energy projects and supporting high-quality development of overseas clean energy through green practices. This approach also extends to project practices in other countries, including South Africa, Côte d'Ivoire, Laos and Poland, where POWERCHINA is integrating ecological protection requirements into the planning, construction and operation phases of a growing number of overseas projects.
